# 1 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 1

---

## Council Notes

**On "land of Kittim" (v.1):** All translators preserve "Kittim" as the traditional designation for the western Mediterranean / Macedonian region. This is a biblical archaism the author deliberately employs to situate the narrative in scriptural categories.

**On "sinful root" / "sinful offshoot" (v.10):** EMET: "sinful root." LOGOS/PNEUMA: "sinful offshoot." The Greek *rhiza hamartolos* means "root of sin" — a plant metaphor indicating corrupted lineage. "Sinful root" is retained as more literal and evocative.

**On "desolating abomination" (v.54):** The Greek *bdelugma eremoseos* echoes Daniel. All translators agree on "desolating abomination" — the standard rendering of a phrase that becomes a key apocalyptic marker.

**On tone:** The chapter is a sustained lament in the style of Lamentations. The passage vv.25-40 is a poetic elegy and should be rendered with heightened register.

---

1. After Alexander son of Philip the Macedonian, who had come forth from the land of Kittim, had struck down Darius king of the Persians and Medes and reigned in his place — he had already reigned over Greece —
2. he fought many battles, captured strongholds, and put kings to death across the earth.
3. He advanced to the ends of the earth and plundered many nations. The earth fell silent before him, and his heart grew proud and arrogant.
4. He assembled an exceedingly strong army and ruled over provinces and nations and rulers, and they became tributaries to him.
5. After all this he fell upon his bed, knowing that he was dying.
6. He summoned his most honored commanders, men who had been raised with him from his youth, and while he was still alive he divided his kingdom among them.
7. Alexander reigned twelve years, and then he died.
8. His commanders each took control of his own region.
9. After his death they all put on crowns, as did their descendants after them for many years; and they multiplied evils upon the earth.
10. From among them there came forth a sinful root — Antiochus Epiphanes, son of King Antiochus, formerly a hostage at Rome — who began to reign in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the Greek kingdom.
11. In those days certain lawless men went out from Israel and led many astray, saying, "Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, for ever since we separated from them many evils have come upon us."
12. This proposal seemed good in their eyes.
13. Some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he granted them authority to follow the ordinances of the nations.
14. They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to Gentile custom,
15. made themselves uncircumcised, abandoned the holy covenant, joined themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.
16. When his kingdom was established before him, Antiochus determined to reign over Egypt, that he might rule over two kingdoms.
17. He invaded Egypt with a strong force — with chariots, war elephants, cavalry, and a great fleet —
18. and made war against Ptolemy king of Egypt. Ptolemy turned and fled before him, and many fell wounded and slain.
19. He captured the fortified cities of Egypt and carried off the plunder of Egypt.
20. Antiochus turned back after his conquest of Egypt, in the one hundred and forty-third year, and advanced against Israel and Jerusalem with a strong force.
21. In his arrogance he entered the sanctuary and took the golden altar, the lampstand for the light with all its equipment,
22. the table of the bread of the Presence, the libation vessels, the cups, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the golden decoration from the facade of the temple — he stripped it all away.
23. He took the silver and the gold and the precious vessels; he also took the hidden treasures wherever he found them.
24. Taking everything, he departed for his own land. He had shed much blood and spoken with great arrogance.
25. And there was great mourning over Israel, in every place.
26. Rulers and elders groaned; young men and maidens grew faint; the beauty of the women faded.
27. Every bridegroom took up a lament; she who sat in the bridal chamber mourned.
28. The land trembled for its inhabitants, and all the house of Jacob was clothed in shame.
29. Two full years later the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah. He came to Jerusalem with a great force
30. and spoke to them words of peace, but in deceit. They trusted him. Then he fell upon the city suddenly, struck it a great blow, and destroyed many of the people of Israel.
31. He plundered the city and set it on fire, tore down its houses and its walls all around.
32. They led away the women and children as captives and seized the livestock.
33. Then they fortified the city of David with a great strong wall and strong towers, and it became their citadel.
34. They installed a garrison of sinful men, lawless men; they strengthened themselves there.
35. They stored arms and provisions and deposited the plunder taken from Jerusalem. It became a grave danger.
36. It lay in ambush against the sanctuary, a constant evil adversary to Israel.
37. They shed innocent blood around the sanctuary on every side and defiled the holy place.
38. The inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them; the city became a dwelling for strangers; she became alien to her own offspring, and her children forsook her.
39. Her sanctuary lay desolate as a wilderness; her feasts became mourning, her sabbaths disgrace, her honor contempt.
40. As great as her glory had been, so great now was her shame; her high dignity was turned into grief.
41. The king then issued a decree throughout his entire kingdom that all peoples should become one people,
42. each abandoning his own customs.
43. All the Gentiles submitted to the king's decree. Many in Israel also accepted his religion willingly; they sacrificed to idols and profaned the sabbath.
44. The king sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, ordering them to follow customs foreign to the land:
45. to prohibit burnt offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings in the sanctuary; to profane sabbaths and feast days;
46. to defile the sanctuary and the holy people;
47. to build altars, sacred precincts, and shrines for idols; to sacrifice pigs and other unclean animals;
48. to leave their sons uncircumcised, and to defile themselves with every manner of uncleanness and profanation,
49. so that they would forget the Torah and abandon all its ordinances.
50. Whoever refused to obey the king's command would die.
51. In accordance with all these words he wrote to his entire kingdom, appointed overseers over all the people, and commanded the cities of Judah to offer sacrifice city by city.
52. Many of the people joined them — all who had forsaken the Torah — and they did evil throughout the land.
53. They drove Israel into hiding in every refuge available to them.
54. On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, they erected the desolating abomination upon the altar of burnt offerings, and throughout the cities of Judah they built pagan altars on every side.
55. At the doors of houses and in the streets they burned pagan incense.
56. The scrolls of the Torah that they found they tore to pieces and burned with fire.
57. Anyone with whom a scroll of the covenant was found, or who followed the Torah — the king's decree condemned him to death.
58. Month after month they brought violent force against every Israelite found in the cities.
59. On the twenty-fifth day of the month they sacrificed on the illicit altar that had been built over the altar of burnt offerings.
60. According to the decree they put to death the women who had circumcised their children,
61. hanging the infants from their mothers' necks; and they executed the members of their households and those who had performed the circumcision.
62. Yet many in Israel stood firm, resolving in their hearts not to eat unclean food.
63. They chose to die rather than to be defiled by food or to profane the holy covenant — and they died.
64. And very great wrath came upon Israel.
